source.title: Random initialisations performing above chance and how to find them
source.authors: Frederik Benzing; Simon Schug; Robert Meier; Johannes von Oswald; Yassir Akram; Nicolas Zucchet; Laurence Aitchison; A. Steger

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether independently initialized networks can be aligned using neuron permutations, but evaluates loss barriers and accuracy along parameter interpolations rather than directly comparing representation distance matrices.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for permutation-aligned parameter interpolation and initialization averaging. It does not report numerical activation-similarity scores. The introduction's citations about representation similarity are prior work, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study matches neuron activations between same-architecture networks trained from different random initialisations. It then checks whether the permuted networks lie in one loss valley. A low barrier after unit matching is indirect, weight-space evidence on V3 (shared learned units across seeds). The study reports no representation-similarity scores and no representation-level map between models, so only V3 is treated as tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors give direct evidence for Entezari et al.'s hypothesis in fully connected nets. For CNNs they state their evidence suggests the hypothesis does not hold, with SGD finding diverse modes at large learning rates.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation matching and Hungarian assignment to find neuron permutations, then evaluates linear parameter interpolation and averaging. It measures loss barriers rather than representation-distance convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture width and depth affect fully connected network barriers; CNN barriers depend notably on learning rate and training regime. Tested activation-matching variants were reported to perform very similarly.

fits_no_version.finding: Permutations found after training put random fully connected initialisations in a shared valley: their averages score above chance, more so with more averaged inits. This does not hold for CNNs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Up to permutation, fully connected networks share a loss valley already at initialisation; CNNs do not.

fits_no_version.finding: L2 vs cosine matching and pre- vs post-nonlinearity activations performed very similarly. Weight matching was slightly worse; small rotations helped slightly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Choice of activation-matching cost has little effect on the quality of permutation alignment.

record.peer_reviewed: OPT2022: 14th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning
record.problems: The reported outcomes are loss barriers and classification performance, not direct comparisons of representation distance matrices. The permutation search is heuristic, and the authors acknowledge that better permutations may exist for narrower networks. Most plotted results do not have exact numerical values in the text; uncertainty is explicitly given for Figure 2 but not for the other plotted findings.
record.rows_left_out: Compact rows capture the principal results and stated condition changes. Left out separate per-width and per-depth plotted points in Figure 2, analogous dataset plots in Figures 6–9, additional CNN settings described in §3.2 and Appendix G, and initialization-scheme and loss-function results in Figure 11; these are mostly figure-only variants of the recorded findings.

untested.parts: No cross-architecture, cross-objective or cross-data comparison. Only a width sweep within the same architecture.

No direct count of shared features or subspaces. The claim that individual units are not shared is not tested by a representation measure, though unit permutation suffices in wide fully connected nets.
No stitching, linear map between representations, relative representations or unpaired alignment. Only parameter-space permutation averaging.
No representation-similarity metric, neighbour count, or out-of-distribution inputs.
No analysis of plateau or of causes of alignment.

missing.what: Linear connectivity after permutation holds across Kaiming, Xavier and Orthogonal initialisation and with MSE loss (V3 observed under these conditions).
Fully connected width/depth sweeps on MNIST and CIFAR10, described as qualitatively similar.

record.verdict_notes: This is weight-space linear mode connectivity, not representation similarity; the link to V3 is indirect. The permutation search is heuristic, so remaining barriers may reflect suboptimal permutations, as the authors acknowledge. All key results are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test alignment across different architectures, objectives, or training data as models scale, or relate alignment to capability.

Tests permutation-aligned loss barriers for same-architecture networks trained from different initializations, not direct counts of shared features or shared subspaces, nor whether individual units recur.
Tests neuron permutations followed by parameter interpolation, not representation stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired inputs.
Does not test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits.
Compares several activation-matching variants, but does not test neighbour-count settings, out-of-distribution inputs, or representation-distance metrics.
Does not isolate shared training data or objectives as causes of alignment, or measure whether alignment plateaus.

rows.subject: fully connected networks
rows.operation_detail: Matched neuron activations across independently trained networks, permuted one network, and compared parameter averages.
rows.measure: Test accuracy of the permuted parameter average; the paper describes the loss barrier as the difference from single-network performance.
rows.baseline: Single Net; unpermuted parameter average also shown
rows.uncertainty: Shaded region is twice the sem (approx. 95% confidence interval) over 6 seeds.
rows.note: The authors state that increasing width eliminates the loss barrier after permutation; this is a width/depth sweep, not a direct representation-distance measurement.
rows.check: Drop V4: the permutation is used to average parameters, not to map one model's representations onto another's. Value is figure-only. The authors say the barrier is 'eliminated completely' in sufficiently wide fully connected nets.

rows.subject: fully connected networks and CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Compared activation-matching variants, including L2 distance versus cosine similarity and activations before versus after the nonlinearity.
rows.measure: Resulting permutation quality, assessed by loss barrier
rows.baseline: Cosine similarity on activations after the nonlinearity, unless otherwise noted
rows.value: The authors state that all variants performed very similarly.
rows.note: The paper reports no meaningful qualitative sensitivity across these tested variants.
rows.check: The variants compared are cost functions inside the permutation-finding algorithm, not similarity measures used to assess convergence. Evidence is one qualitative sentence ('broadly speaking'). Weight matching was slightly worse. Moved to fits_no_version, not V6.

relationships.condition: Wide fully connected networks (Fashion MNIST) and a CNN trained at low learning rate (SGD lr=0.01)
relationships.reason: After activation matching, the permuted average reaches single-network accuracy: barrier eliminated or very small (r1, r5). Figure-only evidence.
relationships.display_finding: Permuted averages reached single-network accuracy, eliminating or nearly eliminating the interpolation barrier.

relationships.condition: Narrow or deeper fully connected nets; CNNs at higher learning rates and in most CNN settings
relationships.reason: Barriers remain after permutation, growing with depth and narrowness and with learning rate in CNNs. Authors infer genuinely diverse solutions (r2, r6, r8, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Barriers persisted after permutation, increasing with depth and narrowness in fully connected networks and with learning rate in CNNs.
